title: Accident Compensation Act 1985
why: Workers' compensation for injuries before 1 July 2014 (legacy claims): weekly payments, impairment, s 134AB serious injury and common law damages, s 135A, and the old contribution and indexation rules.

text.conversion: The Word file was converted to UTF-8 plain text by Legalese Commons (vic_convert.py: stdlib zipfile and ElementTree over word/document.xml). The table of provisions, running heads and footers are dropped; the cover is kept as the file prints it (twice). Each provision starts on its own line with its number; paragraphs are indented two spaces a level; the register's marginal history notes are kept as "[Side note: ...]" lines before the provision they annotate; tables are "| a | b |" rows; Word equations are linearised in place; each embedded equation object or image is marked "[formula ...]" or "[image ...]" and transcribed in accident-compensation-act-1985.formulas.md. The endnotes (amendment history) are kept. Nothing else is changed.
known_conversion_artefacts: the cover (version number, title, number, version date) appears twice at the head, as in the Word file
the "Note" and "Example" labels stand on their own line, unindented, before their text
multi-line formulas set as indented paragraphs keep their brackets but lose their alignment

reconverted_2026_11_07.from: the same Word file, 85-10191a237.docx (sha256 b0a494760613a0e29882add7810454cd8ad9ddaf33ed43196b2e5a2c9743e898), saved by hand on 2026-11-06
reconverted_2026_11_07.why: vic_convert.py dropped every Word <w:sym> character with a code of F000 or more. The register sets several characters that way in the Symbol font: F0D7 its raised decimal point, F0B4 the multiplication sign, F02D the minus sign, F0B7 a bullet; Wingdings boxes were dropped too. vic_convert2.py maps them to the Unicode characters (middle dot, multiplication sign, minus sign, bullet) and Wingdings boxes to "[ ]".
reconverted_2026_11_07.what_changed: 17 lines of the body, nothing else: the notice header is kept exactly as deposited (it still names vic_convert.py, the converter of the 2026-11-06 deposit). Restored: 11 multiplication signs in the s 98C(2) and (3) formulas (e.g. "$11 670 + [(D – 10) × $9940]", "{...} × 1·1"); 11 minus signs in s 91(3)(c), (3A)(c) ("NAL − 10") and the s 98C(3A) formulas (e.g. "[(T − 10) × $2830] + [(10 − P) × $1860]"); 3 decimal points, in s 91(3A)(c) ("0278" read "0·278") and the s 91(10) example ("95%" and "84%" read "9·5%" and "8·4%"). No Symbol-font bullet or Wingdings box had been lost in this Act. Line numbers are unchanged, so the formulas sidecar's line references still hold.
reconverted_2026_11_07.checked: diffed against the 2026-11-06 deposit: only the 17 lines above differ, and only by the restored characters
